idiom_name: concept ExprAlg + struct interpreters + generic program
implementation_notes: The algebra is a C++20 concept over the interpreter type: each interpreter supplies a `repr<T>` member alias (the interpretation type constructor, needed as soon as the DSL is higher-order) and templated members for the constructs, while the program is a generic function or lambda taking the dictionary (`auto&& sym`). What replaces the classic type class: requires-clauses and template instantiation - the concept is a checkable contract, but C++ has no implicit instance resolution, so the dictionary is threaded as an ordinary value or deduced template parameter. Justified when one DSL must have several compile-time interpretations (evaluator, pretty-printer, code generator) and the toolchain is C++20; the interpreters are stateless types, so interpretation costs nothing at run time.
pitfalls: Without the concept (or with a mistyped member) the diagnostics degrade into instantiation backtraces dozens of frames deep - constrain the algebra and the program, not just the interpreter.

Interpreters are types, not type-class instances: any interpreter state must be carried in an object, and the program has to accept it by reference or template parameter - threading it implicitly is impossible.
Each interpreter instantiates the whole program again, so a large algebra with many interpreters multiplies compile time and binary size; keep the algebra small or type-erase deliberately.

variants.name: Template-template-parameter algebra (C++11 and later)
variants.idiom_name: class-template algebra parameterised by template-template parameter
variants.implementation_notes: Before concepts the same encoding is written with a template-template parameter: the algebra is a class template parameterised by the interpretation constructor (`template <template <class> class F>`), each interpreter is a class template passed as the template argument, and the program is a class template over the same parameter. What replaces the classic type class: template-template parameters and static members; the contract is unchecked, so a missing member surfaces as a deep instantiation error rather than a concept violation. Justified on pre-C++20 toolchains and in header-only libraries that must stay portable.
pitfalls: No concept means no early diagnosis: the first error appears at the instantiation that uses the missing member, often inside library code.
Template-template parameters cannot take templates with more parameters than declared, so the interpretation constructor's arity is frozen by the algebra and is awkward to extend.
